title: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
standardsTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
shortTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
description:
Learn a new, short, easy-to-remember sequence every week. That’s 52 sequences a year. Your vocabulary will be enriched, and your partners – super impressed.
Open level
Open-level class means anyone above the Beginner level can attend. However, the class is not catered towards the ‘easy’ though it is meant to be for everyone. You will be challenged no matter your level. It’s a typical combination class, adding proven and well-structured combinations to your repertoire, so keep coming, and one day you will know it all.
New sequence
A new sequence is introduced every week so no worries about not being able to catch up. Of course, you are missing out every time you miss the week, but no risk of not being able to follow what is being introduced. If you have a practice partner, bring her/him with you so you are both on the same page.
Technique Insights
The connection, correct lead and follow, directions of movement, and proper technique are always explained. However, if the movement is absolutely new to you, the explanations might not be sufficient or understandable. This is absolutely normal.
Challenge yourself into listening and trying to understand based on what you already know. Try to find similarities and logic in every movement. This way, you are truly learning and not just being taught.
Immediate Application
Guided Practica Chiquita follows the class immediately so that what you’ve just learned can be immediately implemented into your dance and practiced with practica attendees. If you forgot the steps, then lead the timing – your instructor is present, and you can ask additional questions.
Level of difficulty
In this class, elements from any level can be added to the combination as long as the sequence is short enough to be danced within one or two phrases. It is a good way to familiarize yourself with aspects of tango that are yet unknown to you. To start – mimic what you see. You will learn the technique during regular classes. You can also ask your instructor or higher-level students during Practica.
Inspiration
Sometimes we don’t even know what we don’t know, and we need to be shown what can be done with the elements we have already learned in classes and how they can be combined into beautiful, nicely flowing sequences.

title: BEGINNER CLASSES by TangoAffair
description:
This class is taught by Simonida Cekovic-Vuletic and Svetislav Vuletic, TangoAffair

5 Wednesdays, March 5 – April 2: Argentine Tango for Beginners

7:00 – 8:00pm

Learn the basics of this attractive and sensual dance! Connection, walking, posture, and basic elements like cross, ochos, and simple turns. How to pass and accept (or refuse) the invitation to dance and the etiquette on the social dance floor. This class caters to: 1) complete beginners, 2) dancers with some experience looking to refine their basics, and 3) dancers of all levels interested in exploring the opposite role.

LOCATION: Foundry, 101 Rogers St, Cambridge, MA 02142. Dance Studio, 1st floor. T stops: Kendall/MIT or Lechmere. Plenty of metered parking is available on Third, Fifth, Bent, and Rogers St. You can find a comprehensive map of parking options here.

ADMISSION: $ 120 per person for the whole series or $210 for a couple. The fee is non-refundable and non-transferable.

REGISTRATION: All participants **must register by Monday, March 3. To register please fill out this fFORM **and** transfer the admission amount preferably via Venmo: TangoAffair. Other payment options: PayPal (tangoaffair@gmail.com) or personal check (pay to: Simonida Cekovic-Vuletic, and send the check to 9 Union Street, Cambridge, MA 02139). In case you pay by the check we ask that you text Simonida at 617-615-1550 to tell her that the check is in the mail.

shortTitle: Wednesday Tango Break– 8pm Intermediate Tango Classes
description:
WELCOME FEBRUARY–THE MONTH OF LOVE AND FRIENDSHIP!!

The Tango Society of Boston sponsors Mid-week Tango Dance breaks every Wednesday — Boston’s largest informal Milonga (Tango social dance) and Tango lessons.

7:00-8:00: Beginners Tango with Guillermo Merlo. This class is for beginners and those wishing to brush up some new techniques.
8:00-9:00: Adv-Intermediate Tango Class with Guillermo Merlo –Theme changes every month

This month, the Intermediate+ class wilL work on:
“GANCHOS INTERNOS”. (Inside Ganchos)
“Ganchos Internos” “inside hooks” are movements where one of the partner’s legs hooks around or behind the partner’s leg in a fluid and coordinated manner.
These Ganchos can be done by both the leader and the follower, to create a dynamic and expressive connection during the dance. They are also used to add variety and embellishments to the dance as well as to communicate emotions and sensations during the dance
Because Ganchos Internos require good control of balance, posture and embrace technique to ensure they are performed safely and harmoniously, Maestro Guillermo will review and emphasize the correct techniques to practice to achieve this.

title: Milonga Sal Azul
description:
Dear Tango Friends,

We are thrilled to invite you to Milonga Sal Azul, a warm and vibrant Argentine tango gathering every Thursday night at Blue Salt Restaurant! 💃🕺

What makes it special?
Milonga Sal Azul is a community-driven space where dancers come together to enjoy beautiful tandas, great company, and the magic of tango. Each night offers a unique experience with rotating hosts and talented DJs setting the mood.

📅 Schedule:

  • 7:00 PM – 8:00 PM | Tango Lesson for Beginners ($10)
  • 8:00 PM – 12:00 AM | Milonga ($20, includes a glass of wine 🍷)
  • Enjoy a delicious European fusion dinner in a cozy and inviting setting. Friends and family are welcome to join for dinner or drinks and watch you dance!
  • Plenty of free street parking
  • 5-minute walk from the nearest bus stop

Our goal is to create a BA-style milonga where everyone feels at home—whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just beginning your tango journey.

Come dance with us every Thursday at Blue Salt Restaurant—we can’t wait to share this beautiful experience with you!

Join our community and stay updated by visiting our Facebook group. 💙

With abrazos,
The Milonga Sal Azul Team

title: Tango-Lab : Dancing focused on Musicality/Partnership
description:
Join us Thursday nights for ‘Tango-Lab,’ a unique dance forum tailored for Mid-stage tango dancers and milongueros.  This lab is Dance focused (musicality, Rythym, fluid, partnership) and offers an in-depth exploration of various aspects of the dance.  We take practical patterns, and focus on shared roles, partnership and musicality.

‘Tango Lab’ provides a nurturing space to deepen your understanding, refine your skills, and foster connections within the tango community.

Techniques for Tight turning :

  1. Rotations for Tight Corners (Right ‘With/Con’). Using Tight ocho’s to get out of danger.

  2. Rotations for Tight Corners (Left ‘With/Con’).Using Tight ocho’s to get out of danger (The harder one)

  3. Sacadas for Tight Turns (About Face, and Corners ‘Against/Contra’)

  4. Sacadas for Tight Turns  (Inside with Gancho for Corners ‘Against/Contra’)

Effective Boleos in Tight Spaces

  1. Rotations for Tight Corners (Right ‘With/Con’). Using Tight ocho’s to get out of danger.

  2. Rotations for Tight Corners (Left ‘With/Con’).Using Tight ocho’s to get out of danger (The harder one)

  3. Sacadas for Tight Turns (About Face, and Corners ‘Against/Contra’)

  4. Sacadas for Tight Turns  (Inside with Gancho for Corners ‘Against/Contra’)

Topics will likely include a deviate as need  session of the following topics.
  1. “Gaining real Rhythm “: Overcoming challenges in finding and feeling the rhythm in Tango.
  2. “Feeling the Beat: Tango vs Milonga vs Waltz”: Understanding and distinguishing the unique rhythms of these dance styles.
  3. “Navigating the Lead and Follow Dynamics”: Addressing common 101 challenges and strategies in leading and following.
  4. “The Basic of the Orchestra” : Di Sarli,  D’arienzo, and Pugliese.
  5. “Unlocking Musicality in Dance”: Techniques to interpret and express music in Tango. Getting whats in your head to the partnership.
  6. “The Art of Dancing with Strangers”: Tips and experiences on adapting to new dance partners of all levels
  7. “Maintaining Flow on the Dance Floor”: Strategies for smooth navigation and etiquette in crowded dance spaces.
  8. “Variety vs. Complexity: Keeping Your Partner Engaged with Limited Moves”: Focusing on connection and musicality over a vast repertoire of moves.

THURSDAYS 7:30 – 9pm + Practica
✅ – 50 parking spots available.
✅ – 2 min walk from Oak Grove T stop.
$30/class
✍️ REGISTER HERE: https://UltimateTango.as.me/tango-laboratory

Tango Sueño Academy is the premier Argentine Tango school in Connecticut, serving elite dancers for more than 18 years under the direction of Jorge “Gem” Duras. The group and private lessons focus on authentic Argentine Tango as danced and performed in the halls of Buenos Aires. The classes take place in Stamford, New Haven, Hartford and Danbury metropolitan areas as well as Westchester NY.

Gem has been dancing Argentine Tango for more than 26 years and teaching professionally since 2003. He trains and encourages his students to acquire the proper tango technique, so that they can create the sensuality, musicality and partner connection that the Argentine Tango is famous for.

Although Tango Sueño Academy offers choreography and performance classes for more advanced students, the essence of tango “where the two partners become one” is never forgotten, with the goal of enabling the students to dance with others at local tango events and throughout the world including Buenos Aires.

shortTitle: UT – Open Level –   Flow & Balance – Yoga-Based Tango-Aligned Body Conditioning | Special for Tango Dancers
description:
Move with confidence. Dance with ease.
This 4-week series is designed to help tango dancers develop strength, flexibility, and balance – making every movement feel more fluid, controlled, and effortless.
Through yoga-based conditioning, you’ll improve posture, enhance stability, and deepen your mind-body connection, all while aligning your body for better tango movement.
 Starts Saturday, March 15 at 1:45 PM (Doors open at 1:30 PM)
 Location: Ultimate Tango, 349 Washington Street, Malden
 Bonus: Your class is followed by Che Tango Practica (3–6 PM), the perfect opportunity to apply what you’ve learned!
Why This Is for You
 You want better balance, control, and posture for tango.
 You’re looking to increase flexibility and strength without strain.
 You want to feel more relaxed and grounded in your movements.
 You’re curious how yoga can enhance your tango technique.
Class Details
 Pricing:
Drop-in: $20 per class
Full Workshop: $60 (Save $20!)
 What to Bring:
Your yoga mat and an open mind! No prior yoga experience is needed.
Meet Your Instructor
Hima’s tango journey began with a deep yearning for connection – the effortless harmony between two dancers moving as one. Yet, the more he studied tango, the more he realized that true connection isn’t only about the embrace. It starts within. To truly connect with a partner, one must first be grounded, balanced, and at ease in their own body.
That revelation led him to yoga. Through its practice, he discovered the keys to control, stability, and fluid movement – elements that transformed his tango from the inside out. By refining his own body awareness, he unlocked a deeper, more effortless connection with his dance partners.

Now, Hima shares these transformative insights with fellow dancers – not as distant theory, but as someone who has walked this path himself. He understands the struggles of alignment, posture, and tension because he’s been there.
And now, he offers you the same practical tools and movement techniques that helped him elevate his own tango, so you too can experience greater balance, fluidity, and confidence on the dance floor.
Hima currently teaches at a yoga studio in New Hampshire, where he continues to explore and refine the powerful intersection of yoga and tango.

 Walk in. Dance out. Laugh throughout.
 Saturdays | 3-6 PM
 Ultimate Tango – 349 Washington St, Malden, MA 02155
 FREE PARKING for 50+ cars!
 Just a 3-min walk from Oak Grove T stop (Orange Line).
 What’s in store?
Welcome to Che Tango!, the most laid-back, slightly ridiculous, and irresistibly charming Argentine Tango Practica in town. We dance, we snack, we sip mini beers like it’s 1955 in a forgotten tango bar somewhere between Buenos Aires and your Eastern European grandma’s kitchen.
The tables are dressed in red-checkered plastic, the air smells faintly of good cheese and kielbasa, and the beer flows from large bottles into tiny glasses—just as it should. Expect smooth tangos, clumsy tangos, giggly tangos, and maybe even a polka or two if we get carried away.
Come practice your embrace, argue about technique, and refuel with bread, pickles, and laughter. No pressure, just good old-fashioned fun and great company.
Shoes optional, socks welcome (after all, if you spell “socks” out loud, you get es-o-ke-es—eso qué es? Exactly).
Good humor required. Bring your best tango face and your worst tango excuses.

 Bring a Friend: $20 for both (both leaders or both followers—totally fine!)
 Wear Ridiculous Socks: Get $2 off (One discount per person – no sock bribery loopholes!)
 MUSIC BRIBES (a.k.a. DJ Ransom System)
 Tip $20 = Force the DJ to play traditional tango for 3 tandas.
 Tip $20 = Support the DJ’s “artistic freedom” (aka, neo-tango experiments) for 3 tandas.
 Shoes optional, socks encouraged.
 Good humor required.
 Bring your best tango face and your worst tango excuses.

 See you on the dance floor at Ultimate Tango!

title: TangoLab Mondays (Tango 4w, Val 4w, Milonga 4w)
description:
Detailed info at TOBYTANGO.com

At Tango Lab, we will deepen your connection to tango by cultivating each dancer’s personal musicality and expressive movement, whether you’re a leader or follower. Instead of focusing on specific patterns and steps, we help you develop confidence and clarity in expressing the music through your dance.

• Master the 6 Classic Rhythms, clearly hearing and responding to tango’s foundational pulse. All these can be found in movement you already know.
• Integrate Parallel and Cross Systems with Baldosa and Rotational movements, enriching your dance vocabulary and creativity.
• Develop fluidity and freedom by building a more diverse movement repertoire, allowing authentic self-expression on the dance floor.
• Confidently dance, inspired by iconic orchestras such as Di Sarli, D’Arienzo, and Pugliese.

Weekly Progression:

Week 1 The Core Rhythms in Tango.

Exploring the six classic tango rhythms and finding beauty in fewer patterns with deeper musicality. We’ll master the Long and None rhythms and map patterns on selected songs.

Focus: Single, Doubles, and Zero rhythms – understanding their distinct character and how they form the backbone of tango musical expression.

Featured Music: Di Sarli’s “El Amanecer” / “El Flete” and D’Arienzo’s “Dime Mi Amor”

We’ll discover how these iconic pieces showcase the fundamental tango rhythms and create a foundation for musical expression.

Week 2 is Music with Systems and Rotations
Building on our rhythm work, we’ll integrate these patterns with two movement systems and the two rotation types.

Focus: Moving fluidly between different systems while maintaining rhythmic clarity. Exploring how rotational movements can express the music’s character.

We’ll continue working with the same songs as Week 1, deepening our understanding of how movement systems enhance our musical interpretation.


Week 3 communication and togetherness
This week focuses on exploring communication and togetherness in the dance partnership.

We’ll work on how partners can maintain connection while executing complex rhythmic patterns, and develop a shared sense of musical interpretation.

The emphasis will be on collaborative expression and developing mutual “Cadencia” – the flowing quality that makes tango partnerships magical.


Week 4 attempt to put it all together.

The culmination of our month’s work: discovering orchestral magic by combining rhythms, systems, rotations, and partnership skills.

Focus: Identifying and responding to orchestral voices, understanding the layered complexity of tango music, and developing a personal approach to musicality.

We’ll explore how different orchestras present unique opportunities for expression, and how to adapt your dancing to showcase the character of each piece.

Progressive Monthly Classes:
• Cycle 1: Tango Essentials (4 weeks)
• Cycle 2: Vals (4 weeks)
• Cycle 3: Milonga (4 weeks)

Join us at Tango Lab. Partners are not needed.

title: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
standardsTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
shortTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
description:
Learn a new, short, easy-to-remember sequence every week. That’s 52 sequences a year. Your vocabulary will be enriched, and your partners – super impressed.
Open level
Open-level class means anyone above the Beginner level can attend. However, the class is not catered towards the ‘easy’ though it is meant to be for everyone. You will be challenged no matter your level. It’s a typical combination class, adding proven and well-structured combinations to your repertoire, so keep coming, and one day you will know it all.
New sequence
A new sequence is introduced every week so no worries about not being able to catch up. Of course, you are missing out every time you miss the week, but no risk of not being able to follow what is being introduced. If you have a practice partner, bring her/him with you so you are both on the same page.
Technique Insights
The connection, correct lead and follow, directions of movement, and proper technique are always explained. However, if the movement is absolutely new to you, the explanations might not be sufficient or understandable. This is absolutely normal.
Challenge yourself into listening and trying to understand based on what you already know. Try to find similarities and logic in every movement. This way, you are truly learning and not just being taught.
Immediate Application
Guided Practica Chiquita follows the class immediately so that what you’ve just learned can be immediately implemented into your dance and practiced with practica attendees. If you forgot the steps, then lead the timing – your instructor is present, and you can ask additional questions.
Level of difficulty
In this class, elements from any level can be added to the combination as long as the sequence is short enough to be danced within one or two phrases. It is a good way to familiarize yourself with aspects of tango that are yet unknown to you. To start – mimic what you see. You will learn the technique during regular classes. You can also ask your instructor or higher-level students during Practica.
Inspiration
Sometimes we don’t even know what we don’t know, and we need to be shown what can be done with the elements we have already learned in classes and how they can be combined into beautiful, nicely flowing sequences.

shortTitle: Wednesday Tango Break– 8pm Intermediate Tango Classes
description:
WELCOME FEBRUARY–THE MONTH OF LOVE AND FRIENDSHIP!!

The Tango Society of Boston sponsors Mid-week Tango Dance breaks every Wednesday — Boston’s largest informal Milonga (Tango social dance) and Tango lessons.

Features a lesson in Argentine Tango for Beginning to intermediate dancers (and open to newcomers). No prior experience or partner required.

Schedule
7:00-8:00: Beginners Tango with Guillermo Merlo. This class is for beginners and those wishing to brush up some new techniques.
8:00-9:00: Adv-Intermediate Tango Class with Guillermo Merlo –Theme changes every month

This month, the Intermediate+ class wilL work on:
“GANCHOS INTERNOS”. (Inside Ganchos)
“Ganchos Internos” “inside hooks” are movements where one of the partner’s legs hooks around or behind the partner’s leg in a fluid and coordinated manner.
These Ganchos can be done by both the leader and the follower, to create a dynamic and expressive connection during the dance. They are also used to add variety and embellishments to the dance as well as to communicate emotions and sensations during the dance
Because Ganchos Internos require good control of balance, posture and embrace technique to ensure they are performed safely and harmoniously, Maestro Guillermo will review and emphasize the correct techniques to practice to achieve this.

title: Milonga Sal Azul
description:
Dear Tango Friends,

We are thrilled to invite you to Milonga Sal Azul, a warm and vibrant Argentine tango gathering every Thursday night at Blue Salt Restaurant! 💃🕺

What makes it special?
Milonga Sal Azul is a community-driven space where dancers come together to enjoy beautiful tandas, great company, and the magic of tango. Each night offers a unique experience with rotating hosts and talented DJs setting the mood.

Our goal is to create a BA-style milonga where everyone feels at home—whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just beginning your tango journey.

Come dance with us every Thursday at Blue Salt Restaurant—we can’t wait to share this beautiful experience with you!

Join our community and stay updated by visiting our Facebook group. 💙

With abrazos,
The Milonga Sal Azul Team

Learning Argentine Tango has a couple of phases, and the Beginner course is one of the most crucial components!
In the Beginner course, you will learn all Argentine Tango essentials – a famous tango walk/caminata, baldoza, and 8-count basic to the cross.
You will be explained the essence of tango embrace, how to connect and non-verbally communicate with your partner, how to read the body language, and how to convey the intention, express your needs and take care of the couple’s wellbeing.
You will also become familiar with the principles of improvisation, navigation, and musicality.
 Master the Tango: Conquer the foundation in 8 engaging weeks.
 Unwind & Explore: Discover different genres of tango music.
 Embrace the Community: Learn etiquette and experience the joy of connection on the dance floor.
 Bonus: Gain confidence, improve coordination, reduce stress, and make friends!
Perfect for: Singles & couples, anyone seeking fun & new experiences.

description:
Do you tango? Tango Sueño Academy returns to Hartford area, at the Fred Astaire West Hartford starting April. Join us for weekly Saturday tango!

– 11:30 – 12:30 am: Essentials for all
– 12:30 – 1:30 pm: Intermediate tango
privates by appointment
$25 one hour, $40 both (with monthly registration),
IN APRIL ONLY: first hour $15 (save 40%) second hour $15 ($30 both)
Registration and further details: www.tangosueno.com

__________

Tango Sueño Academy is the premier Argentine Tango school in Connecticut, serving elite dancers for more than 18 years under the direction of Jorge “Gem” Duras. The group and private lessons focus on authentic Argentine Tango as danced and performed in the halls of Buenos Aires. The classes take place in Stamford, New Haven, Hartford and Danbury metropolitan areas as well as Westchester NY.

Gem has been dancing Argentine Tango for more than 26 years and teaching professionally since 2003. He trains and encourages his students to acquire the proper tango technique, so that they can create the sensuality, musicality and partner connection that the Argentine Tango is famous for.

Although Tango Sueño Academy offers choreography and performance classes for more advanced students, the essence of tango “where the two partners become one” is never forgotten, with the goal of enabling the students to dance with others at local tango events and throughout the world including Buenos Aires.

Welcome to Che Tango!, the most laid-back, slightly ridiculous, and irresistibly charming Argentine Tango Practica in town. We dance, we snack, we sip mini beers like it’s 1955 in a forgotten tango bar somewhere between Buenos Aires and your Eastern European grandma’s kitchen.
The tables are dressed in red-checkered plastic, the air smells faintly of good cheese and kielbasa, and the beer flows from large bottles into tiny glasses—just as it should. Expect smooth tangos, clumsy tangos, giggly tangos, and maybe even a polka or two if we get carried away.
Come practice your embrace, argue about technique, and refuel with bread, pickles, and laughter. No pressure, just good old-fashioned fun and great company.
Shoes optional, socks welcome (after all, if you spell “socks” out loud, you get es-o-ke-es—eso qué es? Exactly).
Good humor required. Bring your best tango face and your worst tango excuses.

title: TangoLab Mondays (Tango 4w, Val 4w, Milonga 4w)
description:
Detailed info at TOBYTANGO.com

At Tango Lab, we will deepen your connection to tango by cultivating each dancer’s personal musicality and expressive movement, whether you’re a leader or follower. Instead of focusing on specific patterns and steps, we help you develop confidence and clarity in expressing the music through your dance.

• Master the 6 Classic Rhythms, clearly hearing and responding to tango’s foundational pulse. All these can be found in movement you already know.
• Integrate Parallel and Cross Systems with Baldosa and Rotational movements, enriching your dance vocabulary and creativity.
• Develop fluidity and freedom by building a more diverse movement repertoire, allowing authentic self-expression on the dance floor.
• Confidently dance, inspired by iconic orchestras such as Di Sarli, D’Arienzo, and Pugliese.

Weekly Progression:

Week 1 The Core Rhythms in Tango.

Exploring the six classic tango rhythms and finding beauty in fewer patterns with deeper musicality. We’ll master the Long and None rhythms and map patterns on selected songs.

Focus: Single, Doubles, and Zero rhythms – understanding their distinct character and how they form the backbone of tango musical expression.

Featured Music: Di Sarli’s “El Amanecer” / “El Flete” and D’Arienzo’s “Dime Mi Amor”

We’ll discover how these iconic pieces showcase the fundamental tango rhythms and create a foundation for musical expression.

Week 2 is Music with Systems and Rotations
Building on our rhythm work, we’ll integrate these patterns with two movement systems and the two rotation types.

Focus: Moving fluidly between different systems while maintaining rhythmic clarity. Exploring how rotational movements can express the music’s character.

We’ll continue working with the same songs as Week 1, deepening our understanding of how movement systems enhance our musical interpretation.


Week 3 communication and togetherness
This week focuses on exploring communication and togetherness in the dance partnership.

We’ll work on how partners can maintain connection while executing complex rhythmic patterns, and develop a shared sense of musical interpretation.

The emphasis will be on collaborative expression and developing mutual “Cadencia” – the flowing quality that makes tango partnerships magical.


Week 4 attempt to put it all together.

The culmination of our month’s work: discovering orchestral magic by combining rhythms, systems, rotations, and partnership skills.

Focus: Identifying and responding to orchestral voices, understanding the layered complexity of tango music, and developing a personal approach to musicality.

We’ll explore how different orchestras present unique opportunities for expression, and how to adapt your dancing to showcase the character of each piece.

Progressive Monthly Classes:
• Cycle 1: Tango Essentials (4 weeks)
• Cycle 2: Vals (4 weeks)
• Cycle 3: Milonga (4 weeks)

Join us at Tango Lab. Partners are not needed.

title: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
standardsTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
shortTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
description:
Learn a new, short, easy-to-remember sequence every week. That’s 52 sequences a year. Your vocabulary will be enriched, and your partners – super impressed.
Open level
Open-level class means anyone above the Beginner level can attend. However, the class is not catered towards the ‘easy’ though it is meant to be for everyone. You will be challenged no matter your level. It’s a typical combination class, adding proven and well-structured combinations to your repertoire, so keep coming, and one day you will know it all.
New sequence
A new sequence is introduced every week so no worries about not being able to catch up. Of course, you are missing out every time you miss the week, but no risk of not being able to follow what is being introduced. If you have a practice partner, bring her/him with you so you are both on the same page.
Technique Insights
The connection, correct lead and follow, directions of movement, and proper technique are always explained. However, if the movement is absolutely new to you, the explanations might not be sufficient or understandable. This is absolutely normal.
Challenge yourself into listening and trying to understand based on what you already know. Try to find similarities and logic in every movement. This way, you are truly learning and not just being taught.
Immediate Application
Guided Practica Chiquita follows the class immediately so that what you’ve just learned can be immediately implemented into your dance and practiced with practica attendees. If you forgot the steps, then lead the timing – your instructor is present, and you can ask additional questions.
Level of difficulty
In this class, elements from any level can be added to the combination as long as the sequence is short enough to be danced within one or two phrases. It is a good way to familiarize yourself with aspects of tango that are yet unknown to you. To start – mimic what you see. You will learn the technique during regular classes. You can also ask your instructor or higher-level students during Practica.
Inspiration
Sometimes we don’t even know what we don’t know, and we need to be shown what can be done with the elements we have already learned in classes and how they can be combined into beautiful, nicely flowing sequences.

shortTitle: Wednesday Tango Break– 8pm Intermediate Tango Classes
description:
WELCOME FEBRUARY–THE MONTH OF LOVE AND FRIENDSHIP!!

The Tango Society of Boston sponsors Mid-week Tango Dance breaks every Wednesday — Boston’s largest informal Milonga (Tango social dance) and Tango lessons.

Features a lesson in Argentine Tango for Beginning to intermediate dancers (and open to newcomers). No prior experience or partner required.

Schedule
7:00-8:00: Beginners Tango with Guillermo Merlo. This class is for beginners and those wishing to brush up some new techniques.
8:00-9:00: Adv-Intermediate Tango Class with Guillermo Merlo –Theme changes every month

This month, the Intermediate+ class wilL work on:
“GANCHOS INTERNOS”. (Inside Ganchos)
“Ganchos Internos” “inside hooks” are movements where one of the partner’s legs hooks around or behind the partner’s leg in a fluid and coordinated manner.
These Ganchos can be done by both the leader and the follower, to create a dynamic and expressive connection during the dance. They are also used to add variety and embellishments to the dance as well as to communicate emotions and sensations during the dance
Because Ganchos Internos require good control of balance, posture and embrace technique to ensure they are performed safely and harmoniously, Maestro Guillermo will review and emphasize the correct techniques to practice to achieve this.

Dear Tango Friends,

Our goal is to create a BA-style milonga where everyone feels at home—whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just beginning your tango journey.

Come dance with us every Thursday at Blue Salt Restaurant—we can’t wait to share this beautiful experience with you!

Join our community and stay updated by visiting our Facebook group. 💙

With abrazos,
The Milonga Sal Azul Team

Learning Argentine Tango has a couple of phases, and the Beginner course is one of the most crucial components!
In the Beginner course, you will learn all Argentine Tango essentials – a famous tango walk/caminata, baldoza, and 8-count basic to the cross.
You will be explained the essence of tango embrace, how to connect and non-verbally communicate with your partner, how to read the body language, and how to convey the intention, express your needs and take care of the couple’s wellbeing.
You will also become familiar with the principles of improvisation, navigation, and musicality.
 Master the Tango: Conquer the foundation in 8 engaging weeks.
 Unwind & Explore: Discover different genres of tango music.
 Embrace the Community: Learn etiquette and experience the joy of connection on the dance floor.
 Bonus: Gain confidence, improve coordination, reduce stress, and make friends!
Perfect for: Singles & couples, anyone seeking fun & new experiences.
No prior dance experience required! No partner necessary.

shortTitle: Argentine Tango in West Hartford, CT
description:
Do you tango? Tango Sueño Academy returns to Hartford area, at the Fred Astaire West Hartford starting April. Join us for weekly Saturday tango!

– 11:30 – 12:30 am: Essentials for all
– 12:30 – 1:30 pm: Intermediate tango
privates by appointment
$25 one hour, $40 both (with monthly registration),
IN APRIL ONLY: first hour $15 (save 40%) second hour $15 ($30 both)
Registration and further details: www.tangosueno.com

__________

Tango Sueño Academy is the premier Argentine Tango school in Connecticut, serving elite dancers for more than 18 years under the direction of Jorge “Gem” Duras. The group and private lessons focus on authentic Argentine Tango as danced and performed in the halls of Buenos Aires. The classes take place in Stamford, New Haven, Hartford and Danbury metropolitan areas as well as Westchester NY.

Gem has been dancing Argentine Tango for more than 26 years and teaching professionally since 2003. He trains and encourages his students to acquire the proper tango technique, so that they can create the sensuality, musicality and partner connection that the Argentine Tango is famous for.

Although Tango Sueño Academy offers choreography and performance classes for more advanced students, the essence of tango “where the two partners become one” is never forgotten, with the goal of enabling the students to dance with others at local tango events and throughout the world including Buenos Aires.

Welcome to Che Tango!, the most laid-back, slightly ridiculous, and irresistibly charming Argentine Tango Practica in town. We dance, we snack, we sip mini beers like it’s 1955 in a forgotten tango bar somewhere between Buenos Aires and your Eastern European grandma’s kitchen.

title: TangoLab Mondays (Tango 4w, Val 4w, Milonga 4w)
description:
Detailed info at TOBYTANGO.com

At Tango Lab, we will deepen your connection to tango by cultivating each dancer’s personal musicality and expressive movement, whether you’re a leader or follower. Instead of focusing on specific patterns and steps, we help you develop confidence and clarity in expressing the music through your dance.

• Master the 6 Classic Rhythms, clearly hearing and responding to tango’s foundational pulse. All these can be found in movement you already know.
• Integrate Parallel and Cross Systems with Baldosa and Rotational movements, enriching your dance vocabulary and creativity.
• Develop fluidity and freedom by building a more diverse movement repertoire, allowing authentic self-expression on the dance floor.
• Confidently dance, inspired by iconic orchestras such as Di Sarli, D’Arienzo, and Pugliese.

Weekly Progression:

Week 1 The Core Rhythms in Tango.

Exploring the six classic tango rhythms and finding beauty in fewer patterns with deeper musicality. We’ll master the Long and None rhythms and map patterns on selected songs.

Focus: Single, Doubles, and Zero rhythms – understanding their distinct character and how they form the backbone of tango musical expression.

Featured Music: Di Sarli’s “El Amanecer” / “El Flete” and D’Arienzo’s “Dime Mi Amor”

We’ll discover how these iconic pieces showcase the fundamental tango rhythms and create a foundation for musical expression.

Week 2 is Music with Systems and Rotations
Building on our rhythm work, we’ll integrate these patterns with two movement systems and the two rotation types.

Focus: Moving fluidly between different systems while maintaining rhythmic clarity. Exploring how rotational movements can express the music’s character.

We’ll continue working with the same songs as Week 1, deepening our understanding of how movement systems enhance our musical interpretation.


Week 3 communication and togetherness
This week focuses on exploring communication and togetherness in the dance partnership.

We’ll work on how partners can maintain connection while executing complex rhythmic patterns, and develop a shared sense of musical interpretation.

The emphasis will be on collaborative expression and developing mutual “Cadencia” – the flowing quality that makes tango partnerships magical.


Week 4 attempt to put it all together.

The culmination of our month’s work: discovering orchestral magic by combining rhythms, systems, rotations, and partnership skills.

Focus: Identifying and responding to orchestral voices, understanding the layered complexity of tango music, and developing a personal approach to musicality.

We’ll explore how different orchestras present unique opportunities for expression, and how to adapt your dancing to showcase the character of each piece.

Progressive Monthly Classes:
• Cycle 1: Tango Essentials (4 weeks)
• Cycle 2: Vals (4 weeks)
• Cycle 3: Milonga (4 weeks)

Join us at Tango Lab. Partners are not needed.

title: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
standardsTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
shortTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
description:
Learn a new, short, easy-to-remember sequence every week. That’s 52 sequences a year. Your vocabulary will be enriched, and your partners – super impressed.
Open level
Open-level class means anyone above the Beginner level can attend. However, the class is not catered towards the ‘easy’ though it is meant to be for everyone. You will be challenged no matter your level. It’s a typical combination class, adding proven and well-structured combinations to your repertoire, so keep coming, and one day you will know it all.
New sequence
A new sequence is introduced every week so no worries about not being able to catch up. Of course, you are missing out every time you miss the week, but no risk of not being able to follow what is being introduced. If you have a practice partner, bring her/him with you so you are both on the same page.
Technique Insights
The connection, correct lead and follow, directions of movement, and proper technique are always explained. However, if the movement is absolutely new to you, the explanations might not be sufficient or understandable. This is absolutely normal.
Challenge yourself into listening and trying to understand based on what you already know. Try to find similarities and logic in every movement. This way, you are truly learning and not just being taught.
Immediate Application
Guided Practica Chiquita follows the class immediately so that what you’ve just learned can be immediately implemented into your dance and practiced with practica attendees. If you forgot the steps, then lead the timing – your instructor is present, and you can ask additional questions.
Level of difficulty
In this class, elements from any level can be added to the combination as long as the sequence is short enough to be danced within one or two phrases. It is a good way to familiarize yourself with aspects of tango that are yet unknown to you. To start – mimic what you see. You will learn the technique during regular classes. You can also ask your instructor or higher-level students during Practica.
Inspiration
Sometimes we don’t even know what we don’t know, and we need to be shown what can be done with the elements we have already learned in classes and how they can be combined into beautiful, nicely flowing sequences.

standardsTitle: Wednesday Tango Break– 8pm Intermediate Tango Classes
shortTitle: Wednesday Tango Break– 8pm Intermediate Tango Classes
description:
WELCOME FEBRUARY–THE MONTH OF LOVE AND FRIENDSHIP!!

The Tango Society of Boston sponsors Mid-week Tango Dance breaks every Wednesday — Boston’s largest informal Milonga (Tango social dance) and Tango lessons.

Features a lesson in Argentine Tango for Beginning to intermediate dancers (and open to newcomers). No prior experience or partner required.

Schedule
7:00-8:00: Beginners Tango with Guillermo Merlo. This class is for beginners and those wishing to brush up some new techniques.
8:00-9:00: Adv-Intermediate Tango Class with Guillermo Merlo –Theme changes every month

This month, the Intermediate+ class wilL work on:
“GANCHOS INTERNOS”. (Inside Ganchos)
“Ganchos Internos” “inside hooks” are movements where one of the partner’s legs hooks around or behind the partner’s leg in a fluid and coordinated manner.
These Ganchos can be done by both the leader and the follower, to create a dynamic and expressive connection during the dance. They are also used to add variety and embellishments to the dance as well as to communicate emotions and sensations during the dance
Because Ganchos Internos require good control of balance, posture and embrace technique to ensure they are performed safely and harmoniously, Maestro Guillermo will review and emphasize the correct techniques to practice to achieve this.

description:
Dear Tango Friends,

We are thrilled to invite you to Milonga Sal Azul, a warm and vibrant Argentine tango gathering every Thursday night at Blue Salt Restaurant! 💃🕺

What makes it special?
Milonga Sal Azul is a community-driven space where dancers come together to enjoy beautiful tandas, great company, and the magic of tango. Each night offers a unique experience with rotating hosts and talented DJs setting the mood.

📅 Schedule:

  • 7:00 PM – 8:00 PM | Tango Lesson for Beginners ($10)

Our goal is to create a BA-style milonga where everyone feels at home—whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just beginning your tango journey.

Come dance with us every Thursday at Blue Salt Restaurant—we can’t wait to share this beautiful experience with you!

Join our community and stay updated by visiting our Facebook group. 💙

With abrazos,
The Milonga Sal Azul Team

description:
IN-PERSON BEGINNER ARGENTINE TANGO
Choose from:
– one class experience – 90 min – $40
– four consecutive classes experience – 4×90 min – $120
– 8 weeks course | Each class is 90-min – $199
Tuesdays or Thursdays at 7:30pm.
Free Practica (practice time) follows.
 REGISTER HERE: https://square.link/u/hl9qLyR
Learning Argentine Tango has a couple of phases, and the Beginner course is one of the most crucial components!
In the Beginner course, you will learn all Argentine Tango essentials – a famous tango walk/caminata, baldoza, and 8-count basic to the cross.
You will be explained the essence of tango embrace, how to connect and non-verbally communicate with your partner, how to read the body language, and how to convey the intention, express your needs and take care of the couple’s wellbeing.
You will also become familiar with the principles of improvisation, navigation, and musicality.
 Master the Tango: Conquer the foundation in 8 engaging weeks.
 Unwind & Explore: Discover different genres of tango music.
 Embrace the Community: Learn etiquette and experience the joy of connection on the dance floor.
 Bonus: Gain confidence, improve coordination, reduce stress, and make friends!
Perfect for: Singles & couples, anyone seeking fun & new experiences.
No prior dance experience required! No partner necessary.

Tango Sueño Academy is the premier Argentine Tango school in Connecticut, serving elite dancers for more than 18 years under the direction of Jorge “Gem” Duras. The group and private lessons focus on authentic Argentine Tango as danced and performed in the halls of Buenos Aires. The classes take place in Stamford, New Haven, Hartford and Danbury metropolitan areas as well as Westchester NY.

Gem has been dancing Argentine Tango for more than 26 years and teaching professionally since 2003. He trains and encourages his students to acquire the proper tango technique, so that they can create the sensuality, musicality and partner connection that the Argentine Tango is famous for.

Although Tango Sueño Academy offers choreography and performance classes for more advanced students, the essence of tango “where the two partners become one” is never forgotten, with the goal of enabling the students to dance with others at local tango events and throughout the world including Buenos Aires.

 Walk in. Dance out. Laugh throughout.

 What’s in store?
Welcome to Che Tango!, the most laid-back, slightly ridiculous, and irresistibly charming Argentine Tango Practica in town. We dance, we snack, we sip mini beers like it’s 1955 in a forgotten tango bar somewhere between Buenos Aires and your Eastern European grandma’s kitchen.
The tables are dressed in red-checkered plastic, the air smells faintly of good cheese and kielbasa, and the beer flows from large bottles into tiny glasses—just as it should. Expect smooth tangos, clumsy tangos, giggly tangos, and maybe even a polka or two if we get carried away.
Come practice your embrace, argue about technique, and refuel with bread, pickles, and laughter. No pressure, just good old-fashioned fun and great company.
Shoes optional, socks welcome (after all, if you spell “socks” out loud, you get es-o-ke-es—eso qué es? Exactly).

title: TangoLab Mondays (Tango 4w, Val 4w, Milonga 4w)
description:
Detailed info at TOBYTANGO.com

At Tango Lab, we will deepen your connection to tango by cultivating each dancer’s personal musicality and expressive movement, whether you’re a leader or follower. Instead of focusing on specific patterns and steps, we help you develop confidence and clarity in expressing the music through your dance.

• Master the 6 Classic Rhythms, clearly hearing and responding to tango’s foundational pulse. All these can be found in movement you already know.
• Integrate Parallel and Cross Systems with Baldosa and Rotational movements, enriching your dance vocabulary and creativity.
• Develop fluidity and freedom by building a more diverse movement repertoire, allowing authentic self-expression on the dance floor.
• Confidently dance, inspired by iconic orchestras such as Di Sarli, D’Arienzo, and Pugliese.

Weekly Progression:

Week 1 The Core Rhythms in Tango.

Exploring the six classic tango rhythms and finding beauty in fewer patterns with deeper musicality. We’ll master the Long and None rhythms and map patterns on selected songs.

Focus: Single, Doubles, and Zero rhythms – understanding their distinct character and how they form the backbone of tango musical expression.

Featured Music: Di Sarli’s “El Amanecer” / “El Flete” and D’Arienzo’s “Dime Mi Amor”

We’ll discover how these iconic pieces showcase the fundamental tango rhythms and create a foundation for musical expression.

Week 2 is Music with Systems and Rotations
Building on our rhythm work, we’ll integrate these patterns with two movement systems and the two rotation types.

Focus: Moving fluidly between different systems while maintaining rhythmic clarity. Exploring how rotational movements can express the music’s character.

We’ll continue working with the same songs as Week 1, deepening our understanding of how movement systems enhance our musical interpretation.


Week 3 communication and togetherness
This week focuses on exploring communication and togetherness in the dance partnership.

We’ll work on how partners can maintain connection while executing complex rhythmic patterns, and develop a shared sense of musical interpretation.

The emphasis will be on collaborative expression and developing mutual “Cadencia” – the flowing quality that makes tango partnerships magical.


Week 4 attempt to put it all together.

The culmination of our month’s work: discovering orchestral magic by combining rhythms, systems, rotations, and partnership skills.

Focus: Identifying and responding to orchestral voices, understanding the layered complexity of tango music, and developing a personal approach to musicality.

We’ll explore how different orchestras present unique opportunities for expression, and how to adapt your dancing to showcase the character of each piece.

Progressive Monthly Classes:
• Cycle 1: Tango Essentials (4 weeks)
• Cycle 2: Vals (4 weeks)
• Cycle 3: Milonga (4 weeks)

Join us at Tango Lab. Partners are not needed.

title: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
standardsTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
shortTitle: Short Sequences – enrich your vocabulary with 52 sequences every year
description:
Learn a new, short, easy-to-remember sequence every week. That’s 52 sequences a year. Your vocabulary will be enriched, and your partners – super impressed.
Open level
Open-level class means anyone above the Beginner level can attend. However, the class is not catered towards the ‘easy’ though it is meant to be for everyone. You will be challenged no matter your level. It’s a typical combination class, adding proven and well-structured combinations to your repertoire, so keep coming, and one day you will know it all.
New sequence
A new sequence is introduced every week so no worries about not being able to catch up. Of course, you are missing out every time you miss the week, but no risk of not being able to follow what is being introduced. If you have a practice partner, bring her/him with you so you are both on the same page.
Technique Insights
The connection, correct lead and follow, directions of movement, and proper technique are always explained. However, if the movement is absolutely new to you, the explanations might not be sufficient or understandable. This is absolutely normal.
Challenge yourself into listening and trying to understand based on what you already know. Try to find similarities and logic in every movement. This way, you are truly learning and not just being taught.
Immediate Application
Guided Practica Chiquita follows the class immediately so that what you’ve just learned can be immediately implemented into your dance and practiced with practica attendees. If you forgot the steps, then lead the timing – your instructor is present, and you can ask additional questions.
Level of difficulty
In this class, elements from any level can be added to the combination as long as the sequence is short enough to be danced within one or two phrases. It is a good way to familiarize yourself with aspects of tango that are yet unknown to you. To start – mimic what you see. You will learn the technique during regular classes. You can also ask your instructor or higher-level students during Practica.
Inspiration
Sometimes we don’t even know what we don’t know, and we need to be shown what can be done with the elements we have already learned in classes and how they can be combined into beautiful, nicely flowing sequences.

shortTitle: Wednesday Tango Break– 8pm Intermediate Tango Classes
description:

The Tango Society of Boston sponsors Mid-week Tango Dance breaks every Wednesday — Boston’s largest informal Milonga (Tango social dance) and Tango lessons.

8:00-9:00: Adv-Intermediate Tango Class with Guillermo Merlo –Theme changes every month

This month, the Intermediate+ class wilL work on:
“GANCHOS INTERNOS”. (Inside Ganchos)
“Ganchos Internos” “inside hooks” are movements where one of the partner’s legs hooks around or behind the partner’s leg in a fluid and coordinated manner.
These Ganchos can be done by both the leader and the follower, to create a dynamic and expressive connection during the dance. They are also used to add variety and embellishments to the dance as well as to communicate emotions and sensations during the dance
Because Ganchos Internos require good control of balance, posture and embrace technique to ensure they are performed safely and harmoniously, Maestro Guillermo will review and emphasize the correct techniques to practice to achieve this.

We are thrilled to invite you to Milonga Sal Azul, a warm and vibrant Argentine tango gathering every Thursday night at Blue Salt Restaurant! 💃🕺

What makes it special?
Milonga Sal Azul is a community-driven space where dancers come together to enjoy beautiful tandas, great company, and the magic of tango. Each night offers a unique experience with rotating hosts and talented DJs setting the mood.

📅 Schedule:

  • 7:00 PM – 8:00 PM | Tango Lesson for Beginners ($10)
  • 8:00 PM – 12:00 AM | Milonga ($20, includes a glass of wine 🍷)
  • Enjoy a delicious European fusion dinner in a cozy and inviting setting. Friends and family are welcome to join for dinner or drinks and watch you dance!
  • Plenty of free street parking
  • 5-minute walk from the nearest bus stop

Our goal is to create a BA-style milonga where everyone feels at home—whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just beginning your tango journey.

Come dance with us every Thursday at Blue Salt Restaurant—we can’t wait to share this beautiful experience with you!

Join our community and stay updated by visiting our Facebook group. 💙

With abrazos,
The Milonga Sal Azul Team

Learning Argentine Tango has a couple of phases, and the Beginner course is one of the most crucial components!
In the Beginner course, you will learn all Argentine Tango essentials – a famous tango walk/caminata, baldoza, and 8-count basic to the cross.
You will be explained the essence of tango embrace, how to connect and non-verbally communicate with your partner, how to read the body language, and how to convey the intention, express your needs and take care of the couple’s wellbeing.
You will also become familiar with the principles of improvisation, navigation, and musicality.
 Master the Tango: Conquer the foundation in 8 engaging weeks.
 Unwind & Explore: Discover different genres of tango music.
 Embrace the Community: Learn etiquette and experience the joy of connection on the dance floor.
 Bonus: Gain confidence, improve coordination, reduce stress, and make friends!
Perfect for: Singles & couples, anyone seeking fun & new experiences.
No prior dance experience required! No partner necessary.

title: Film Screening ‘Tango Malhar’
description:
Saya Date (MIT class of 2015) took her first tango class at MIT many years ago to fulfill a PE requirement, not realizing that tango would find her again much later in life—and change it profoundly. Today, she is a filmmaker and dancer, and she recently completed her debut feature film Tango Malhar, which follows a young rickshaw driver in India who stumbles into the world of Argentine tango.

The film premiered last month at BAFICI, Buenos Aires’ premier film festival, and the MIT Tango Club is thrilled to host Saya and screen her film for the MIT and the greater Boston tango community. Saya will also host a Q&A and discuss the film’s journey and how tango has shaped her own.

Watch film trailer here.

For event details and tickets, visit following link: https://sites.google.com/site/mittangoclub/events/film-screening-tango-malhar?authuser=0

title: Saturday Tango Breakfast
description:
Boston’s newest organizer and TDJ is bringing tango life to the am. Nam Nguyen is organizing a tango breakfast. Not just any breakfast, a Vietnamese one. Time for those early birds in the community to thrive. Start your Saturday with a delicious morning meal, coffee, and a rejuvenating practica.
Have you been putting off meeting up for coffee or breakfast with one or two of your non-tango friends? Make plans with them now for May 31st. Brian and Andi will be teaching a beginner friendly class from 9:30am – 10:am. They will also be at the practica to assist you in your tango practice.
Logistics:
Date/Time: May 31st
Practica 9am – 12pm
Class 9:30am – 10:30am
Private lesson slots available to book with either one of the teachers or both after 10:30am.
Breakfast till out of stock
Address: 1548 Dorchester Avenue, Dorchester, MA 02124, 2nd Floor
Price:
Practica $20*
Class + Practica $30*
*50% off for students
Payment: Cash, Venmo, or Zelle
Private lessons reach out to Andi/Brian
About the teachers: https://www.abtango.com/
Andi Babbs is an instructor at Ultimate Tango. She has intensively studied with Anita Flejter and Hernan Brizuela. Over the years, she’s learned from dozens of tango artists worldwide. She has visited Buenos Aires multiple times, and while there, she has taken many workshops with tango maestros. In addition, she’s been a guest teacher at various places in the USA. Her enthusiasm is unparalleled. When she’s not at her home studio, she can be found exchanging ideas, continuing her tango learning, performing, and teaching tango. She is also the host of Andi-longa and a Tango DJ. https://www.ultimatetango.com/team
Brian Spellman Argentine Tango found Brian when he was working as a nightshift janitor at a soda factory in Connecticut, feeling quite directionless. Soon enough, he was getting all of his work done in two hours so he could spend the rest of his shift practicing the steps, or passing out in a closet to build energy for dancing at the next opportunity. Several trips to Buenos Aires and many wonderful teachers later, Tango has the ultimate grip on Brian’s soul, and he’s happier for it. He is currently an instructor in Florence, MA, on the Western MA Tango Board, Tango DJ, performer, and has been a guest instructor in various places in the USA.
About the DJ:
Nam Nguyen shadows musicology with his sister (a Composition PhD student at Florida State University) and with Tango DJs and musicians in the Tango community. He helped arrange scores and curate music for a documentary. Nam learns Tango with various instructors. His goal is to understand the essence of Argentine Tango orchestral music (i.e. the substances in the music that make people move), to revive the forgotten Vietnamese Tango melodies with danceable arrangements.

Registration and further details: www.tangosueno.com

__________

Tango Sueño Academy is the premier Argentine Tango school in Connecticut, serving elite dancers for more than 18 years under the direction of Jorge “Gem” Duras. The group and private lessons focus on authentic Argentine Tango as danced and performed in the halls of Buenos Aires. The classes take place in Stamford, New Haven, Hartford and Danbury metropolitan areas as well as Westchester NY.

Gem has been dancing Argentine Tango for more than 26 years and teaching professionally since 2003. He trains and encourages his students to acquire the proper tango technique, so that they can create the sensuality, musicality and partner connection that the Argentine Tango is famous for.

Although Tango Sueño Academy offers choreography and performance classes for more advanced students, the essence of tango “where the two partners become one” is never forgotten, with the goal of enabling the students to dance with others at local tango events and throughout the world including Buenos Aires.

title: UT – Open Level –  CHE TANGO! – Saturday Afternoon Practica at ULTIMATE TANGO
standardsTitle: UT – Open Level –  CHE TANGO! – Saturday Afternoon Practica at ULTIMATE TANGO
shortTitle: UT – Open Level –  CHE TANGO! – Saturday Afternoon Practica at ULTIMATE TANGO
description:
CHE TANGO! – Saturday Afternoon Practica at ULTIMATE TANGO 
 Walk in. Dance out. Laugh throughout.
 Saturdays | 3-6 PM
 Ultimate Tango – 349 Washington St, Malden, MA 02155
 FREE PARKING for 50+ cars!
 Just a 3-min walk from Oak Grove T stop (Orange Line).
 What’s in store?
Welcome to Che Tango!, the most laid-back, slightly ridiculous, and irresistibly charming Argentine Tango Practica in town. We dance, we snack, we sip mini beers like it’s 1955 in a forgotten tango bar somewhere between Buenos Aires and your Eastern European grandma’s kitchen.
The tables are dressed in red-checkered plastic, the air smells faintly of good cheese and kielbasa, and the beer flows from large bottles into tiny glasses—just as it should. Expect smooth tangos, clumsy tangos, giggly tangos, and maybe even a polka or two if we get carried away.
Come practice your embrace, argue about technique, and refuel with bread, pickles, and laughter. No pressure, just good old-fashioned fun and great company.
Shoes optional, socks welcome (after all, if you spell “socks” out loud, you get es-o-ke-es—eso qué es? Exactly).
Good humor required. Bring your best tango face and your worst tango excuses.
 PRICING:
 Entry: $15
 Bring a Friend: $20 for both (both leaders or both followers—totally fine!)
 Wear Ridiculous Socks: Get $2 off (One discount per person – no sock bribery loopholes!)
 MUSIC BRIBES (a.k.a. DJ Ransom System)
 Tip $20 = Force the DJ to play traditional tango for 3 tandas.
 Tip $20 = Support the DJ’s “artistic freedom” (aka, neo-tango experiments) for 3 tandas.
 Shoes optional, socks encouraged.
 Good humor required.
 Bring your best tango face and your worst tango excuses.
 Tag your tango friends! The more, the merrier… or at least, the weirder.
 See you on the dance floor at Ultimate Tango!
MORE INFO: https://www.ultimatetango.com/che-tango

title: UT – Advanced Level – Elevating Technique, Connection, and Expression – couples only only
standardsTitle: UT – Advanced Level – Elevating Technique, Connection, and Expression – couples only only
shortTitle: UT – Advanced Level – Elevating Technique, Connection, and Expression – couples only only
description:
This exclusive, invitation-only course for couples is designed for experienced tango dancers seeking to refine their skills and elevate their dance to the next level. With a strong focus on precision, connection, and improvisation, this ongoing program will help you integrate advanced tango elements seamlessly into your movement while maintaining balance, fluidity, and musicality.
Each class will delve into intricate giros, advanced sacadas, enrosques, planeos, changes of direction, and dynamic musical interpretation, all while honing technique and deepening partner connection. The curriculum emphasizes controlled axis, refined torsions, and weight transfer, ensuring that each movement is executed with clarity and confidence.
This course is by invitation only and open exclusively to couples who are comfortable with foundational tango mechanics and ready to explore more sophisticated techniques. To inquire about participation, please email ultimateTango@gmail.com for more information.
The classes are held at 349 Washington St, Malden, MA 02148.

title: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
standardsTitle: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
shortTitle: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
description:
Sacada means displacement

Back sacadas require all the tango technique normally necessary to perform regular displacement plus a good understanding of torsions, pivots, timing, and movement delay.

Torsions, pivots, over-pivoting
We will work on torsions, pivots, over pivoting (without disturbing your partner axis and losing connection and balance), ability to walk while in overturned position, plus other necessary elements so the back sacada can be freely introduced during the improvised dance.

READ MORE: https://www.ultimatetango.com/preadvanced

title: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
standardsTitle: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
shortTitle: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
description:
A challenge

We can be happy once we speak conversational Tango, or we can yearn for more. If Tango is like language – there surely there must be more! And it is!

Tango never stops. And that’s the beauty of it. There is always more. And as we become more and more comfortable with the fundamentals, navigation, musicality, new element, and different styles, we look for more.

The advanced course challenges you to a more elaborate exploration of more advanced tango elements. Each 4 weeks cycle is focused on introducing new intricate variations, investigating new possibilities, and mastering combinations involving elements originally introduced to you during the pre-Advanced courses.

PLEASE NOTE: The Advanced level freely mixes all elements taught in the Pre-Advanced level and adds more variations. Please be considerate – if you have difficulties with basic to the cross or molinete, call boleo a bolero, and gancho a gaucho – PLEASE do not register for this class. Once you are at this level, you won’t appreciate people randomly showing up and defying the whole purpose of this class. THANK YOU!

REGISTER HERE: https://UltimateTango.as.me/Advanced-Course-May2023

description:
WELCOME FEBRUARY–THE MONTH OF LOVE AND FRIENDSHIP!!

The Tango Society of Boston sponsors Mid-week Tango Dance breaks every Wednesday — Boston’s largest informal Milonga (Tango social dance) and Tango lessons.

Features a lesson in Argentine Tango for Beginning to intermediate dancers (and open to newcomers). No prior experience or partner required.

Schedule
7:00-8:00: Beginners Tango with Guillermo Merlo. This class is for beginners and those wishing to brush up some new techniques.
8:00-9:00: Adv-Intermediate Tango Class with Guillermo Merlo –Theme changes every month

This month, the Intermediate+ class wilL work on:
“GANCHOS INTERNOS”. (Inside Ganchos)
“Ganchos Internos” “inside hooks” are movements where one of the partner’s legs hooks around or behind the partner’s leg in a fluid and coordinated manner.
These Ganchos can be done by both the leader and the follower, to create a dynamic and expressive connection during the dance. They are also used to add variety and embellishments to the dance as well as to communicate emotions and sensations during the dance
Because Ganchos Internos require good control of balance, posture and embrace technique to ensure they are performed safely and harmoniously, Maestro Guillermo will review and emphasize the correct techniques to practice to achieve this.

title: Milonga Sal Azul
description:
Dear Tango Friends,

We are thrilled to invite you to Milonga Sal Azul, a warm and vibrant Argentine tango gathering every Thursday night at Blue Salt Restaurant! 💃🕺

description:
Do you tango? Tango Sueño Academy returns to Hartford area, at the Fred Astaire West Hartford starting April. Join us for weekly Saturday tango!

privates by appointment

Registration and further details: www.tangosueno.com

__________

Tango Sueño Academy is the premier Argentine Tango school in Connecticut, serving elite dancers for more than 18 years under the direction of Jorge “Gem” Duras. The group and private lessons focus on authentic Argentine Tango as danced and performed in the halls of Buenos Aires. The classes take place in Stamford, New Haven, Hartford and Danbury metropolitan areas as well as Westchester NY.

Gem has been dancing Argentine Tango for more than 26 years and teaching professionally since 2003. He trains and encourages his students to acquire the proper tango technique, so that they can create the sensuality, musicality and partner connection that the Argentine Tango is famous for.

Although Tango Sueño Academy offers choreography and performance classes for more advanced students, the essence of tango “where the two partners become one” is never forgotten, with the goal of enabling the students to dance with others at local tango events and throughout the world including Buenos Aires.

title: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
standardsTitle: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
shortTitle: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
description:
Sacada means displacement

Back sacadas require all the tango technique normally necessary to perform regular displacement plus a good understanding of torsions, pivots, timing, and movement delay.

Torsions, pivots, over-pivoting
We will work on torsions, pivots, over pivoting (without disturbing your partner axis and losing connection and balance), ability to walk while in overturned position, plus other necessary elements so the back sacada can be freely introduced during the improvised dance.

READ MORE: https://www.ultimatetango.com/preadvanced

title: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
standardsTitle: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
shortTitle: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
description:
A challenge

We can be happy once we speak conversational Tango, or we can yearn for more. If Tango is like language – there surely there must be more! And it is!

Tango never stops. And that’s the beauty of it. There is always more. And as we become more and more comfortable with the fundamentals, navigation, musicality, new element, and different styles, we look for more.

The advanced course challenges you to a more elaborate exploration of more advanced tango elements. Each 4 weeks cycle is focused on introducing new intricate variations, investigating new possibilities, and mastering combinations involving elements originally introduced to you during the pre-Advanced courses.

PLEASE NOTE: The Advanced level freely mixes all elements taught in the Pre-Advanced level and adds more variations. Please be considerate – if you have difficulties with basic to the cross or molinete, call boleo a bolero, and gancho a gaucho – PLEASE do not register for this class. Once you are at this level, you won’t appreciate people randomly showing up and defying the whole purpose of this class. THANK YOU!

REGISTER HERE: https://UltimateTango.as.me/Advanced-Course-May2023

The Tango Society of Boston sponsors Mid-week Tango Dance breaks every Wednesday — Boston’s largest informal Milonga (Tango social dance) and Tango lessons.

Features a lesson in Argentine Tango for Beginning to intermediate dancers (and open to newcomers). No prior experience or partner required.

8:00-9:00: Adv-Intermediate Tango Class with Guillermo Merlo –Theme changes every month

This month, the Intermediate+ class wilL work on:
“GANCHOS INTERNOS”. (Inside Ganchos)
“Ganchos Internos” “inside hooks” are movements where one of the partner’s legs hooks around or behind the partner’s leg in a fluid and coordinated manner.
These Ganchos can be done by both the leader and the follower, to create a dynamic and expressive connection during the dance. They are also used to add variety and embellishments to the dance as well as to communicate emotions and sensations during the dance
Because Ganchos Internos require good control of balance, posture and embrace technique to ensure they are performed safely and harmoniously, Maestro Guillermo will review and emphasize the correct techniques to practice to achieve this.

shortTitle: Argentine Tango in West Hartford, CT
description:
Do you tango? Tango Sueño Academy returns to Hartford area, at the Fred Astaire West Hartford starting April. Join us for weekly Saturday tango!

– 11:30 – 12:30 am: Essentials for all
– 12:30 – 1:30 pm: Intermediate tango
privates by appointment
$25 one hour, $40 both (with monthly registration),
IN APRIL ONLY: first hour $15 (save 40%) second hour $15 ($30 both)
Registration and further details: www.tangosueno.com

__________

Tango Sueño Academy is the premier Argentine Tango school in Connecticut, serving elite dancers for more than 18 years under the direction of Jorge “Gem” Duras. The group and private lessons focus on authentic Argentine Tango as danced and performed in the halls of Buenos Aires. The classes take place in Stamford, New Haven, Hartford and Danbury metropolitan areas as well as Westchester NY.

Gem has been dancing Argentine Tango for more than 26 years and teaching professionally since 2003. He trains and encourages his students to acquire the proper tango technique, so that they can create the sensuality, musicality and partner connection that the Argentine Tango is famous for.

Although Tango Sueño Academy offers choreography and performance classes for more advanced students, the essence of tango “where the two partners become one” is never forgotten, with the goal of enabling the students to dance with others at local tango events and throughout the world including Buenos Aires.

title: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
standardsTitle: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
shortTitle: UT Pre-Advanced Argentine Tango – Learn Back Sacadas
description:
Sacada means displacement

Back sacadas require all the tango technique normally necessary to perform regular displacement plus a good understanding of torsions, pivots, timing, and movement delay.

Torsions, pivots, over-pivoting
We will work on torsions, pivots, over pivoting (without disturbing your partner axis and losing connection and balance), ability to walk while in overturned position, plus other necessary elements so the back sacada can be freely introduced during the improvised dance.

READ MORE: https://www.ultimatetango.com/preadvanced

title: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
standardsTitle: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
shortTitle: UT Advanced Argentine Tango – Elaborate exploration
description:
A challenge

We can be happy once we speak conversational Tango, or we can yearn for more. If Tango is like language – there surely there must be more! And it is!

Tango never stops. And that’s the beauty of it. There is always more. And as we become more and more comfortable with the fundamentals, navigation, musicality, new element, and different styles, we look for more.

The advanced course challenges you to a more elaborate exploration of more advanced tango elements. Each 4 weeks cycle is focused on introducing new intricate variations, investigating new possibilities, and mastering combinations involving elements originally introduced to you during the pre-Advanced courses.

PLEASE NOTE: The Advanced level freely mixes all elements taught in the Pre-Advanced level and adds more variations. Please be considerate – if you have difficulties with basic to the cross or molinete, call boleo a bolero, and gancho a gaucho – PLEASE do not register for this class. Once you are at this level, you won’t appreciate people randomly showing up and defying the whole purpose of this class. THANK YOU!

REGISTER HERE: https://UltimateTango.as.me/Advanced-Course-May2023

description:

The Tango Society of Boston sponsors Mid-week Tango Dance breaks every Wednesday — Boston’s largest informal Milonga (Tango social dance) and Tango lessons.

8:00-9:00: Adv-Intermediate Tango Class with Guillermo Merlo –Theme changes every month

This month, the Intermediate+ class wilL work on:
“GANCHOS INTERNOS”. (Inside Ganchos)
“Ganchos Internos” “inside hooks” are movements where one of the partner’s legs hooks around or behind the partner’s leg in a fluid and coordinated manner.
These Ganchos can be done by both the leader and the follower, to create a dynamic and expressive connection during the dance. They are also used to add variety and embellishments to the dance as well as to communicate emotions and sensations during the dance
Because Ganchos Internos require good control of balance, posture and embrace technique to ensure they are performed safely and harmoniously, Maestro Guillermo will review and emphasize the correct techniques to practice to achieve this.

title: Milonga Sal Azul
description:
Dear Tango Friends,

We are thrilled to invite you to Milonga Sal Azul, a warm and vibrant Argentine tango gathering every Thursday night at Blue Salt Restaurant! 💃🕺

What makes it special?
Milonga Sal Azul is a community-driven space where dancers come together to enjoy beautiful tandas, great company, and the magic of tango. Each night offers a unique experience with rotating hosts and talented DJs setting the mood.

Our goal is to create a BA-style milonga where everyone feels at home—whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just beginning your tango journey.

Come dance with us every Thursday at Blue Salt Restaurant—we can’t wait to share this beautiful experience with you!

Join our community and stay updated by visiting our Facebook group. 💙

title: Argentine Tango in West Hartford, CT
standardsTitle: Argentine Tango in West Hartford, CT
shortTitle: Argentine Tango in West Hartford, CT
description:
Do you tango? Tango Sueño Academy returns to Hartford area, at the Fred Astaire West Hartford starting April. Join us for weekly Saturday tango!

– 11:30 – 12:30 am: Essentials for all
– 12:30 – 1:30 pm: Intermediate tango
privates by appointment
$25 one hour, $40 both (with monthly registration),
IN APRIL ONLY: first hour $15 (save 40%) second hour $15 ($30 both)
Registration and further details: www.tangosueno.com

__________

Tango Sueño Academy is the premier Argentine Tango school in Connecticut, serving elite dancers for more than 18 years under the direction of Jorge “Gem” Duras. The group and private lessons focus on authentic Argentine Tango as danced and performed in the halls of Buenos Aires. The classes take place in Stamford, New Haven, Hartford and Danbury metropolitan areas as well as Westchester NY.

Gem has been dancing Argentine Tango for more than 26 years and teaching professionally since 2003. He trains and encourages his students to acquire the proper tango technique, so that they can create the sensuality, musicality and partner connection that the Argentine Tango is famous for.

Although Tango Sueño Academy offers choreography and performance classes for more advanced students, the essence of tango “where the two partners become one” is never forgotten, with the goal of enabling the students to dance with others at local tango events and throughout the world including Buenos Aires.

description:
Sacada means displacement

Back sacadas require all the tango technique normally necessary to perform regular displacement plus a good understanding of torsions, pivots, timing, and movement delay.

Torsions, pivots, over-pivoting
We will work on torsions, pivots, over pivoting (without disturbing your partner axis and losing connection and balance), ability to walk while in overturned position, plus other necessary elements so the back sacada can be freely introduced during the improvised dance.
